questions.questionText: What does LCEL's .pipe() composition actually give you, beyond just running steps in sequence?
options: Nothing extra — it's purely a stylistic way to write sequential code
The whole pipeline automatically supports invoke, stream, and batch, without extra code for each
It automatically fine-tunes the model on your data
It removes the need for a prompt template
questions.correctAnswer: The whole pipeline automatically supports invoke, stream, and batch, without extra code for each
questions.explanation: Because every LCEL component shares a common interface, composing them together yields a pipeline that supports invoke/stream/batch for free, without hand-writing that logic for each stage.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a prompt template in LangChain?
options: It separates the fixed prompt text from the variable data that fills it in, similar to a parameterized query
It replaces the need for a chat model
It automatically translates the prompt into other languages
It only works with output parsers, not models
questions.correctAnswer: It separates the fixed prompt text from the variable data that fills it in, similar to a parameterized query
questions.explanation: A prompt template takes a plain object of variables and produces a fully-formed message, keeping prompt structure separate from the specific data used to fill it.

questions.questionText: Why can you typically swap one chat model provider for another in a LangChain pipeline with minimal changes?
options: You can't — every provider requires a completely different chain
All chat models implement the same invoke/stream/batch interface, so the rest of the chain doesn't need to change
LangChain automatically converts between providers' APIs behind the scenes with no shared interface
Only Anthropic models work with LCEL
questions.correctAnswer: All chat models implement the same invoke/stream/batch interface, so the rest of the chain doesn't need to change
questions.explanation: LangChain's uniform chat model interface is what makes providers largely interchangeable within an existing chain.
